Activity.description: What the turn is doing right now (spinner text).

AgentProblemInfo.description: A definition file that failed to parse.

versions.description: Version numbers on the active path.

annotations.description: MCP hints; informational only, never trusted for decisions (t13).

form.description: JSON Schema of the form to fill.

subagent.description: Labels prompts raised by a subagent (D47).

AskAnswer.description:
The answer to an ask: the result of the `permission.ask` request, and the body of
`permission.respond` (minus `ask_id`).

message.description: `reject` with a message sends it to the model as feedback (02 §7 step 5).

AskKind.description: Ask kinds a client can render (02 §7).

AskParams.description: Daemon → client request `permission.ask`; the result is an [`AskAnswer`].

oneOf.description: The turn ended (interrupt, failure) while the ask was open: resolved as `cancel`.

BackgroundToolParams.description:
Move a running tool call out of the foreground (ticket 43). Only `shell` acts on it:
the command keeps running as a background job and the turn continues.

backgrounded.description: False when that call isn't running in the current turn.

size.description: Total blob size, so readers know when to stop.

control.description:
`agent` ("Genie is browsing"), `user` ("you're in control"),
`waiting_for_approval`, or `handoff` (the agent asked the user to take over).

BrowserFileChooser.description:
A file picker the page opened during take-over (SA-24). The client shows a native file
dialog and answers with `browser.file_chooser.answer`.

w.description: Viewport width in CSS pixels (`browser.input` coordinates are in `0..w`).

CancelRequest.description:
`$/cancelRequest`: the daemon withdraws a request it sent (e.g. an ask answered
elsewhere, or the lease moved).

Channel.description: A release stream. Each channel has its own binaries, data dir, socket and DB (D40).

Citation.description: A citation span on a text part (D36).

ClientRef.description: A client as named in leases, ask resolutions and `daemon.status` (02 §5).

label.description: Human label shown on the "Take over" banner, e.g. "Desktop" or "CLI (pid 4211)".

immediate.description: A `client` command that runs as soon as it is picked, even during a turn.

CommandListParams.description:
`command.list`: by `session_id`, or by `kind` (+ `project_id` / `workspace_path`)
before a session exists.

diagnostics.description: Skipped files, name clashes with built-ins, unreachable MCP servers.

CommandRoute.description: What a client does with a command (06 §9.1).

oneOf.description: Sent as a `command` input part; the reply streams.
Opens the client's own UI or calls a method; never a model turn.

CommandSource.description: Where a command comes from; also its lookup order (built-ins win).

ConfigSchemaResult.description: JSON Schema of the config plus Settings UI metadata (D23, D34).

ConfigScope.description:
Config write scopes (D23). `policy` is only ever a *source*, never a target.
`managed` labels definitions delivered by managed policy (e.g. MCP servers); it is
never a write target either.

ConfigSource.description: Where a config value came from.

ConnectedClient.description: One connected client as `daemon.status` reports it.

degraded.description: Served in degraded mode because the daemon is older and busy (01 §4.2).

text.description: The page's selected text (empty when nothing is selected).

Cost.description: Cost in US dollars, as estimated from the catalog prices (D27).

code_execution.description: Per-chat provider code execution toggle (D35; default off).

web_search.description: Per-chat provider web search toggle (06 §8; default on).

hint.description: Last 4 characters of a key, or the account name.

DeleteAllBeginResult.description: What "Delete all data" will remove (04 §8), and the token that confirms it.

clears_audit.description: Whether the local audit log is removed too (kept under a managed audit policy).

token.description: Pass to `data.delete_all.confirm` within `expires_in_s` seconds; single use.

Delivery.description: How a prompt is delivered to a session (01 §5.2).

oneOf.description: Injected at the next step boundary of a running turn, or starts a turn if idle.
A new turn after the current turn settles.

confirm.description: First call without it returns the "what will run" manifest; second call installs.

manifest.description: Commands, URLs and permissions the entry will use.

Empty.description: `{}` params or result. Unknown fields are ignored (02 §10).

ErrorInfo.description: A user-facing error: stable code, message, optional fix link (01 §7).

ExportResult.description: Either a blob (large exports) or inline text.

FileChooserAnswerParams.description: `browser.file_chooser.answer`: the files the user picked; empty cancels.

siblings.description: For each message on the path with siblings: the sibling ids, in order.

note.description:
What the user still has to do (e.g. the commands that open a pull request when
the engine doesn't push itself).

Id.description: Request id. Genie clients use numbers; strings are accepted for other tools.

ImportParams.description:
Importer (D53, 07 §5); the report shapes are owned by spec 07. `options`:
`{cwd?, source?: "claude-code"|"claude-desktop"|"opencode", level?: "user"|"project",
selected?: [item id], confirm_append?: bool}`. `scan`/`preview` return
`{items: [...]}`, `apply` returns the saved report `{date, items, path}`.

InboxChanged.description: The queue shown above the composer: the full current list.

InitializeParams.description: Client → daemon; must be the first request on a connection.

client_instance_id.description: Stable per app install/window; used for lease reclaim (02 §5).

protocol.description: Semver of `genie-protocol` the client was built with.

restart_pending.description: Version-skew path (01 §4.2): the daemon will drain and exit; re-run ensure.

text.description: Composition text; empty ends the composition.

oneOf.description:
A `/` command with the `prompt` route (06 §9.1): `name` without the slash
(`explore`, `git:pr`, `server:prompt`), `args` the rest of the line. The engine
stores the expansion when the message is admitted.

interrupted.description: False when no turn was running.

LeaseLost.description: `lease.lost` (02 §5): sent to the old driver on `take_over` or when the lease lapses.

LiveStatus.description: Ephemeral status reported live; a superset of [`SessionStatus`].

oneOf.description: `AwaitingAsk` with no client attached; an OS notification was raised.

McpItemsResult.description: `mcp.tools` / `mcp.resources` / `mcp.prompts`: MCP's own list items, passed through.

cost.description: Assistant messages: estimated cost of that step (D27).

source.description:
User-role messages Genie wrote (`synthetic`: a background job finished, a resume
note …), so clients show them as notices, not as the user's words. Absent = the user.

usage.description: Assistant messages: the tokens of the step that produced this message.

ModelInfo.description:
Model as merged from catalog + discovery + overrides (D27). The full catalog
record lives in `extra` until spec 03 fixes the client-facing subset.

NavigateParams.description:
`browser.navigate`: the user's own navigation in the Browser tab. It never prompts
(research §4.2) and launches the browser and opens a tab when none exists.

tab_id.description: Defaults to the active tab (a new one when the session has none).

url.description: What the user typed: a URL, `host[:port]` (https, http for localhost) or `about:blank`.

Part.description: A stored message part, final value (`part.ended`).

text.description: Readable summary; may be empty when the provider only returns opaque data.

provider_executed.description: Server-side tool (web search, code execution) run by the provider (D36).

content.description: Text, JSON or rich parts; spilled results carry `spill_ref` instead (D32).

oneOf.description: Compaction boundary (D33): our summary text, or a provider checkpoint.
A part type this client does not know (02 §10).

PartKind.description: Which kind of streamed part a `part.started` opens.

locked.description: Cannot be removed with `permissions.rules.remove` (managed policy, CLI layer).

source.description: The settings file the rule is in, or `policy` / `session`.

PermissionRuleScope.description: Where a permission rule lives (06 §5.4, D23).

oneOf.description: Remembered for one session only ("always" with session scope).

cwd.description: Folder whose project/local layers to read (Code workspaces).

scope.description: Only this scope; omit for every scope.

session_id.description: Session whose session-scoped and CLI rules to include.

Preview.description: What the ask card shows for a permission ask.

ProjectFileInfo.description: One file in a project's knowledge (`project.file.list`).

tokens.description: Estimated tokens of the extracted text.

client_msg_id.description: Idempotency key: a retry with the same id returns the first result.

parent_id.description: Edit = prompt with `parent_id` set to the edited message's parent (D24).

ResolvedBy.description: Who resolved an ask (`permission.resolved.by`): a client, or an automatic source.

RespondParams.description:
The answer to an ask: the result of the `permission.ask` request, and the body of
`permission.respond` (minus `ask_id`).

message.description: `reject` with a message sends it to the model as feedback (02 §7 step 5).

ResyncRequired.description:
`session.resync_required` (02 §3.1). With `snapshot`, reload with `session.get`
and subscribe from its `head_seq`; otherwise re-subscribe with `after_seq = from_seq`.

RuleScope.description: Scopes a saved permission rule can go to (t13).

oneOf.description: Who drives the agent browser (05 §9 banner), ephemeral.
A page opened a file picker while the user is in control (SA-24), ephemeral.
An event type from a newer daemon. Skip it.

SessionImportParams.description: `session.import`: the session JSON from a file path or a blob (`blob.put.*`).

remapped.description: Some ids already existed and were replaced by new ones.

SessionKind.description: Session kind: Chat or Code mode (D54).

SessionSettingsOverlay.description:
Session-only settings (the CLI layer, D23 layer 2): `--allow`/`--deny` rules,
`--settings <file>` and `--add-dir`. They apply to this session only.

add_dirs.description: Extra directories the session may read/edit without asking (`--add-dir`).

enable_browser.description: `--enable-browser`: browser tools in a headless session (SA-28c).

settings_path.description: A settings file read by the daemon (same user) as the session's CLI layer.

SessionSummary.description: One row in the session list (02 §6.2, workspace feed).

SessionUpdated.description: Only the changed fields are present.

StatusEvent.description:
Live status. `state` is the session state machine (01 §5.1); `activity` the finer
spinner state of 02 §4.2.

after_seq.description: Omit to replay from the start of the retained log.

TabNewParams.description: `browser.tab.new`: a tab the user opened (`about:blank` without `url`); it becomes active.

error.description:
Why a `blocked` call was blocked: `code` is `policy_blocked` for managed policy
(with "Blocked by <org> policy (rule)"), `GENIE-TOOL-BLOCKED` for a deny rule.

TrustedFolder.description:
One stored folder decision (`trust.json`, 08 §4). Revoke with
`trust.set {path, decision: "revoke"}`.

approvals.description: Approved project definitions (MCP servers, hooks) under this decision.

identity.description: Repository identity the decision is bound to, if any.

message_id.description: The admitted user message (or inbox item id until the store assigns messages).

project_id.description: Move a Chat session into a project; `""` moves it out of its project.

Usage.description: Token usage of a step or session.

keys.description: One value per `group_by` entry, in order.

UserNotification.description:
`notification`: something the desktop app should show as an OS notification
(e.g. "Genie needs your approval", 02 §7 step 2).

pending_asks.description: Asks waiting across all sessions (badge count).

WorktreeFinishResult.description: `worktree.finish` result (additive: older clients read it as `{}`).

message.description: What happened, for the user (PR commands, why a branch was kept …).
